title: Incoming morphisms of a distinguished triangle form a cofiltered cofinal index category
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] and let $S$ be a saturated multiplicative system compatible with its triangulated structure [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. For a distinguished triangle $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$, let $\mathcal I$ be the category whose objects are morphisms of triangles $(s,s',s''):(X',Y',Z',f',g',h')\to(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ from a distinguished triangle, with $s,s',s''\in S$, and whose morphisms $(X'',Y'',Z'')\to(X',Y',Z')$ are morphisms of triangles with all three components in $S$ compatible with the given morphisms to $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$. Then $\mathcal I$ is cofiltered, and each projection $\mathcal I\to S/X$, $\mathcal I\to S/Y$, and $\mathcal I\to S/Z$ is initial (the cofiltered form of cofinal).

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 (lemma-limit-triangles), dual cofiltered form

proof.text: Let $t:X_0\to X$ be an object of $S/X$. The triangle-completion lemma [lem-pur-triangle-completion-ms6-05r9] supplies a distinguished triangle $(X_0,Y_0,Z_0)$ and a morphism of triangles $(t,t',t'')$ to $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ with $t',t''\in S$, i.e. an object of $\mathcal I$ whose projection to $S/X$ is $t$; the identity of $t$ is then a morphism in $S/X$ from that projection to $t$. Thus $\mathcal I\to S/X$ satisfies the existence condition (1) of initiality, and by the $Y$- and $Z$-forms of the same lemma so do $\mathcal I\to S/Y$ and $\mathcal I\to S/Z$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 proof, construction over a prescribed denominator

proof.text: $\mathcal I$ is nonempty: by MS1 of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization] the identity morphism of $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ is an object. Given two objects of $\mathcal I$, the first assertion of the common-refinement lemma [lem-pur-triangle-common-refinement-ms3-05r9] gives an object of $\mathcal I$ with an arrow to each of them; given two parallel arrows of $\mathcal I$, its second assertion gives an arrow into their common source after which they agree. Hence $\mathcal I$ is cofiltered.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 proof, filteredness condition (2)

proof.text: Initiality of $\mathcal I\to S/X$, condition (2) (Stacks' initial functor, the notion used by the cofinality lemma 0A1S; here a zigzag of length two suffices). Let $t:X_0\to X$ be an object of $S/X$, let $x_1,x_2$ be objects of $\mathcal I$ with $X$-components $s_1:X_1\to X$, $s_2:X_2\to X$, and let $u_i:X_i\to X_0$ be morphisms of $S/X$, so $t\circ u_i=s_i$. By the first assertion of the common-refinement lemma [lem-pur-triangle-common-refinement-ms3-05r9] there are an object $x_3$ of $\mathcal I$, with $X$-component $s_3:X_3\to X$, and arrows $x_3\to x_i$ in $\mathcal I$ with $X$-components $a_i:X_3\to X_i$, so $s_i\circ a_i=s_3$. Then $t\circ(u_1\circ a_1)=s_3=t\circ(u_2\circ a_2)$ with $t\in S$, so the second clause of MS3 in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization] gives $v:X_4\to X_3$ in $S$ with $u_1\circ a_1\circ v=u_2\circ a_2\circ v$. The triangle-completion lemma [lem-pur-triangle-completion-ms6-05r9], applied to the distinguished triangle $(X_3,Y_3,Z_3)$ of $x_3$ and to $v$, gives a distinguished triangle $(X_4,Y_4,Z_4)$ and a morphism of triangles $(v,v',v'')$ to $(X_3,Y_3,Z_3)$ with all components in $S$; composing with the structure morphism of $x_3$ (MS1) gives an object $x_4$ of $\mathcal I$ and an arrow $x_4\to x_3$. The composite arrows $x_4\to x_1$ and $x_4\to x_2$ satisfy $u_1\circ a_1\circ v=u_2\circ a_2\circ v$ on $X$-components, which is condition (2) for $\mathcal I\to S/X$ with the zigzag $x_1\leftarrow x_4\rightarrow x_2$. Rotation of distinguished triangles (TR2), together with MS5 to identify $S/X[1]$ with $S/X$, identifies $\mathcal I$ with the corresponding categories for $(Y,Z,X[1],g,h,-f[1])$ and $(Z,X[1],Y[1],h,-f[1],-g[1])$ compatibly with the projections, so the same argument gives condition (2) for $\mathcal I\to S/Y$ and $\mathcal I\to S/Z$.

split_report.summary: Split the 05R9 categorical claim into two supporting statements: completion of a prescribed S-denominator to a morphism of distinguished triangles, and common refinement/equalization of triangle morphisms. The item proof then derives cofilteredness and initiality of all three projections from those helpers and the definitions of the saturated triangulated localization.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the Lemma 05SC proof clause asserting that the category I of triangle morphisms is cofiltered and cofinal over X/S, Y/S, and Z/S.
